Company Description
Theta Neurotech is developing a wearable EEG patch designed to predict epileptic seizures 30–60 minutes before onset. The company focuses on improving quality of life for the 1.1 million Americans and 30 million people globally living with drug-resistant epilepsy. By enabling preventative drug deployment, Theta Neurotech aims to reduce seizure-related risks and support more independent lifestyles. Applicants will join an early-stage team working at the intersection of neuroscience, medical devices, and advanced machine learning to build clinically meaningful technology.
Role Description
The Fractional Machine Learning Lead will provide part-time technical leadership for the design, development, and optimization of ML and deep learning models that power Theta Neurotech’s seizure prediction system. Day-to-day responsibilities include defining model architectures, implementing and evaluating algorithms, and collaborating with product and clinical partners to translate EEG data into robust predictive insights. The role also involves establishing best practices for data preprocessing, feature engineering, experimentation, and deployment, as well as mentoring team members and contributing to technical roadmaps. This is a part-time hybrid role based in Chicago, IL, with a mix of on-site collaboration and work-from-home flexibility.
Qualifications
Strong foundation in Computer Science, including data structures, algorithms, and software engineering principles.
Hands-on experience in Machine Learning and Deep Learning, with a track record of building and deploying models in production or research settings.
Proficiency in Statistics for experimental design, model evaluation, and analysis of noisy physiological or time-series data.
Ability to design and optimize Algorithms for large-scale or real-time inference, preferably in signal processing or biomedical applications.
Advanced programming skills in languages such as Python, and experience with ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow).
Experience working with time-series, biosignal, or EEG data, and familiarity with healthcare or regulated environments is beneficial.
Effective communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to cross-functional partners and document decisions clearly.
Graduate-level degree (MS or PhD) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

Keep the GTM stack (Salesforce, HubSpot, Asana, the dashboard) connected and trustworthy through automation, not hands-on administration.

A CS or adjacent degree (or equivalent demonstrated ability); post-school engineering experience optional but valued
You ship production code - TypeScript/React and Python, or can get there fast
You use AI coding and agent tools daily, and want a whole organization working that way
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills

Bias to action and comfort with ambiguity. “I'll just build it” is a real option, and you want the hard, high-ownership tour this role is

title: Data Engineer

description_preview:
About Us
Campfire builds modern ERP software for finance teams — bringing accounting, close, and reporting into one fast, intuitive system. We're a small, senior team obsessed with craft, speed, and making complex financial software feel simple.
About The Role 🌟
ERP implementations are one of the hardest unsolved problems in enterprise software. They're historically slow, manual, and consultant-heavy — months of spreadsheets, mapping documents, and billable hours. At Campfire, we're building AI agents to automate the heavy lifting and cut implementations from months to weeks.
As a Data Engineer, you'll be an architect of the agentic platform at the heart of that effort: the system that moves customers onto Campfire and keeps their financial data live and in sync once they're there. It's the machinery that determines how fast the company scales — every improvement you ship compounds across every future implementation.
This is not a traditional data engineering role. You won't be writing SQL inside someone else's ETL tool. You'll be building the platform itself, and the AI agents that run on it, with real ownership over what you build and work that ships to customers fast.
💼 We Need Someone Who
Designs and builds pipelines that move customer financial data reliably from source systems (ERPs, data warehouses, payment systems, etc) into Campfire — and keep it flowing once customers are live
Ships major features on the AI agent that drives customer implementations, expanding what it can handle autonomously
Partners with the implementation team to understand real customer data — what it looks like, what it means, and how it needs to transform — and turn those insights into platform capabilities
As you grow, contribute to Ember, the shared agent stack powering Campfire's AI products beyond data integration
👥 Ideal Candidate
Strong full-stack engineering fundamentals — our stack is Python, NextJS/React — and comfort building frameworks and tooling, not just the business logic inside them
Experience building and operating data pipelines. Snowflake experience is a plus, but not a requirement
Experience building AI agents or LLM-powered systems is a strong plus
Self-driven and autonomous — we trust you to take the reins, manage your own work, and lead projects to the finish line
Comfortable with agility and ambiguity — the team is lean and moves fast, and some of our hardest problems, like live data integration, don't have established playbooks yet. You'll help write them
📢 Let's Connect
Think you're the perfect fit? We're excited to meet you! Reach out, share your story, and let's explore how you can ignite change at Campfire.
❤️‍🩹 Benefits
We provide top decile benefits including 100% premium coverage for employees and 80% coverage for dependents with comprehensive healthcare and dental care options.

SCE offers a great benefits package complete with medical, dental, and vision insurance, health savings account health reimbursement account, flexible spending account, employer paid life and disability, 401(k) matching, and paid time off along with other essential benefits.
This position will report to our office location in Knoxville, TN.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities
The Essential Duties and Responsibilities are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties, but not all duties performed for this position. Other duties may be assigned.
Preparing and reviewing project specific preconstruction plans (i.e., Accident Prevention Plans, Quality Control Plans, Environmental Protection Plans, Transportation Plans, etc.) and other applicable documents for compliance with contract plans and technical specifications.
Reviewing design plans and technical specifications for technical and constructability evaluations and assisting with estimating to support proposal preparation and construction or civil activities.
Prepare project specific product data and material submittals.
Supervising safety and health activities, applicable safety and health requirements in work methods, and methods for inspecting the work to ensure safety and health measures and instructions are being applied properly which comply with contract design and technical specifications, project specific accident prevention plans, and Federal, state, and local laws, rules, and regulations.
Performing quality control inspections, preparing daily reports, and scheduling and performing three phases of control on definable features of work as defined by contract design plans and technical specifications.
Implementing and managing quality control system in accordance with the contract technical specifications and project specific quality control plan (i.e., USACE Remote Management System and NAVFAC Electronic Construction Management System).
Setting up surveying equipment and surveying features to assist with the generation of project model, topography, as-built drawings, etc. and to assist with surveying and construction layout for large earthwork and drainage projects (i.e., roadways, site development, landfills, dams, levees, streams, storm water facilities, etc.).
Assisting field management team members on various projects and providing input on problem solving.
Assisting engineers, project managers, and other project team members with specific design plan and technical specification requirements.
Minimum Qualifications
To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The qualifications listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required.
Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering or Construction Management or equivalent field of study.
0-3 years of experience in the field of civil engineering.
Ability to perform quantity takeoffs for various types of construction and civil projects and proposals using on-screen and manual take-off tools based on an accurate reading of plans or blueprints, geotechnical reports, requests for proposals, and related documents, and transferring data into software for review with others.
Ability to review request for proposal package documentation, design plans and technical specifications to determine scope of work and required contents of estimate for request for proposals, request for information, and subcontractor cost quotes.
Understand basic surveying process and can communicate with land surveyors and construction personnel on a regular basis.
Familiar with current industry standards and practices.
10-40% travel is required.

Employees must always maintain a constant state of mental alertness and situational awareness. Essential and marginal functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for bending, stooping, sitting, walking, or standing for prolonged periods of time. Majority of time is spent sitting in a comfortable position with frequent opportunity to move about. Work is mostly performed from a sedentary posture. The employee is regularly required to hear, talk, sit, and use hands and fingers to operate a mouse, keyboard, and phone. The employee may be occasionally required to reach with hands and arms and lift, handle, or move objects weighing up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust vision.

Delta Defense is seeking a **Data Engineer** to help transform complex data into reliable, actionable insights that support business decisions. description_preview:
Company Overview
Swarm Defense Technologies designs and builds small unmanned aircraft systems for the U.S. Department of Defense. We are headquartered in Auburn Hills, Michigan, where electrical design, firmware, machining, assembly, and flight test all happen under one roof. Our current work is focused on moving production-ready small UAS from prototype to volume delivery on compressed program timelines, and we are building the engineering and manufacturing team to do it.
Job Summary
Swarm Defense is hiring a UAS Engineer who has spent years designing, building, and flying drones and wants to do it for a living on aircraft that get fielded. This is a generalist role. On a given week you might be laying out a new airframe, integrating a flight controller and payload, tuning a control loop, building a test article, or standing on the flight line running the test card and diagnosing why the aircraft did not do what it was supposed to. If you have built and flown your own aircraft, crashed them, figured out why, and built them better, that is the background we are looking for. We care more about what you have flown than what is on your resume.
You will join a small engineering team where the same people design, build, and fly the aircraft, and you will own a piece of the aircraft end to end. You will work directly with our mechanical, electrical, and embedded engineers and with the production floor. Our design-to-flight cycle is measured in weeks, not quarters.
Key Responsibilities
Design and integrate small UAS subsystems: airframe, propulsion, power, flight controller, sensors, payload, and communication links.
Build prototype and test aircraft by hand, from initial bring-up through flight-ready configuration.
Plan and execute flight tests: write test cards, fly or direct flights, capture data, and turn results into design changes.
Configure and tune flight control stacks (PX4, ArduPilot, or similar), including parameter tuning, failsafes, and mission behavior.
Diagnose flight anomalies from logs, telemetry, and hardware inspection; run root cause to closure.
Select and qualify components (motors, ESCs, props, batteries, radios, sensors) against performance and reliability requirements.
Produce the drawings, wiring diagrams, BOMs, and build instructions needed for production to build what you tested.
Maintain the aircraft fleet, ground control equipment, and test infrastructure so testing is never blocked on hardware.
Follow and improve flight safety procedures and range operations for testing.
Requirements
Demonstrated experience designing, building, and flying multirotor or fixed-wing UAS, professional or personal. You must be able to show us aircraft you have built and explain the design decisions.
Hands-on with the full small-UAS stack: airframe, motors/ESCs, power systems, flight controllers, radios, and GPS/IMU sensors.
Working knowledge of PX4, ArduPilot, Betaflight, or comparable flight control firmware, including configuration and log analysis.
Competent with common build tools and methods: soldering, crimping, basic machining or 3D printing, CAD.
Able to methodically troubleshoot a system that spans mechanical, electrical, and software domains.
BS in aerospace, mechanical, electrical engineering or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated experience.
Bonus Points
FAA Part 107 certificate and real flight hours on aircraft you built.
Experience with UAS at 5 kg or above, fixed-wing or VTOL platforms, or autonomous mission flight.
Ability to read and modify flight controller firmware or write ground-side tooling (C/C++, Python).
Experience with RF systems, video links, or mesh radios.
Competitive or club drone experience (racing, freestyle, long-range, or university UAS teams).
Defense, aerospace, or other regulated hardware environment.
Prior exposure to flight testing under a written test plan and safety review.
Benefits
Health Insurance: We cover 100% of health insurance premiums for our employees.
401(k): Company retirement plan with employer match.
﻿
Swarm Defense is an early-stage defense company, and the pace is set by what the mission requires. The work is hands-on: engineers build what they design, test it on real aircraft, and own the result. Timelines are short, feedback from the field is direct, and problems get solved by the people closest to them.
We reward initiative and give people ownership of their area. If you want to see your work fly within weeks rather than years, and you are comfortable operating without a large support structure around you, this is the right environment.

description_preview:
About BJAK
The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.
Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.
Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.
We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.
If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.
The Role
We are looking for mobile developers to build BJAK's AI Neobank App across Android and iOS.
This role is for strong mobile builders who can ship clean, reliable and intuitive mobile experiences, whether their main strength is Android, iOS or both.
What You'll Own
Build and ship mobile features for Android and/or iOS.
Create simple mobile flows for insurance, payments, claims, renewals and financial services.
Work with product, design and backend teams to turn complex journeys into usable mobile products.
Integrate APIs and handle edge cases, loading states, errors and production issues.
Improve app performance, reliability, crash rate and user experience.
Support fast product launches, experiments and iterations across mobile journeys.
Help set high standards for mobile product quality across the app.
What We're Looking For
3+ years of mobile development experience in Android, iOS or both.
Strong experience with Kotlin and/or Swift.
Experience shipping production apps used by real users.
Strong product sense and attention to mobile UX.
Able to work with APIs, analytics, crash logs and production feedback.
Fast, practical and comfortable owning work with limited handholding.
App links, GitHub, screenshots or examples of shipped work are a strong advantage.
The Kind of Builder We Want

About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
The
Ground Systems
(Mission) Software Engineer II
is responsible for Varda's critical ground segment software, and the platform it runs on which enables spacecraft operations. We operate at the intersection of telemetry and commanding, data acquisition and distribution, mission control interfaces, simulation and test automation, with reliable deployment across lab, test range, and mission operations environments. You'll work hands-on with flight software, avionics, RF/ground systems, and mission ops.
Responsibilities
Own Ground Segment Services: Develop and maintain high-reliability services for telemetry ingestion, scaling, distribution, and commanding. Ensure deterministic behavior for real-time operations and post-flight analysis.

Standardize CI/CD pipelines, artifact management, service templates, infrastructure-as-code, simulation and hardware-in-the-loop frameworks, test harnesses, and observability - all delivered as self-service tooling.
Deployments Across Environments: Create robust deployment patterns for lab benches, test stands, and mission networks. Implement safe rollout/rollback strategies and air-gapped or limited-connectivity deployment approaches.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science, math, physics, engineering or equivalent technical experience in safety critical software.
3+ years of experience in the development of spacecraft or similar safety critical software.
Expertise with development in Python, along with a strong understanding of the language concepts.
Have strong systems fundamentals: concurrency, networking, performance, reliability.
Experience building real-time data acquisition, scaling, and distribution services - low-latency messaging, time-series and relational stores.
Hands-on experience with CI/CD, dependency/build systems, and infrastructure-as-code.
End-to-end observability experience: logging, metrics, tracing.
Docker/Kubernetes; release management, phased rollouts, and operational readiness for controlled networks.
Preferred Skills And Experience
Proficiency in C++, Ansible, and/or NiceGUI.
Experience with DAQ and closed-loop control (lab/test control environments).
Prior work on CI/testing/simulation/data tools integrated with flight software teams.
Experience with requirements, test, and certification artifacts from safety-critical or certified workflows.
Knowledge of ground systems standards; security in mission networks.
Experience building mission-grade UIs with structured command workflows, alarming, and situational awareness.

About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
The
Systems Engineer II, Avionics
oversees the design, integration, and testing of avionics systems for our Winnebago Spaceship. They ensure that all systems are ready for both launch and operational phases, requiring a deep understanding of avionics system design, manufacturing processes, and operational protocols. They closely collaborate with various engineering teams and navigate conflicting requirements to achieve seamless system integration. Their expertise will be crucial in ensuring the vehicle meets its mission objectives, from space manufacturing to hypersonic testing during reentry.
Responsibilities
Collaborate with cross functional teams to define project scopes and initial requirements, guiding designs from concept to prototype and full-scale production.
Develop electrical architecture, system diagrams, and budgets to account for power, telemetry, channel count, size, and mass predictions used to communicate closing vehicle solutions to company level objectives.
Analyze architecture for potential faults and risks, develop comprehensive mitigation plans, resolve uncertainties, and collaborate on Fault Detection Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) or operational workarounds when hardware solutions are unfeasible.
Conduct comprehensive verification plans for avionics systems on flight and HITL hardware, ensuring readiness for launch and compliance with mission objectives for space and reentry operations.
Participate in mission operations as an Avionics specialist or system operator, where they’ll determine system health, suggest corrective actions to reentry commit criteria for operational success.
Oversee the integration of the Winnebago avionics systems, acting as the primary point of contact for integrated systems investigations.
Design, build, and operate the Hardware In The Loop (HITL) testbeds, simulating the spacecraft on the ground to ensure all systems are mission ready.
Develop avionics ground infrastructure, support the design and integration of test racks and R&D equipment used to power and communicate with the flight vehicles. Contribute to developing engineering best practices, focusing on increased test automation and efficiency.
Draw from their experiences to help mentor and train new engineers, fostering a culture of learning and continuous improvement within the team.
Basic Qualifications
Education: Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field.
Experience: 3+ years of experience in system design, test planning, and validation.
Programming Skills: Proficiency in programming and debugging with Python.
Technical Expertise: Experience with power supplies, modular DAQ systems, RTD and 4-20mA devices, and general test equipment.
Preferred Skills And Experience
Proven experience taking vehicle electrical systems from concept to operational production.
Prior experience setting up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and conducting system level tests.
Familiarity with Unix environments and the ability to use command line utilities.
Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.
Strong project or program management skills.
Relevant prior roles: Avionics Hardware, FPGA Engineer, Electronics Test Engineer, Electrical Systems Engineer
Pay Range
Salary range: Engineer II: $119,543 - $152,749/ per year.
This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA.
Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance.
You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards
